text:
Sam Carter: Quick follow-up from the RFC thread — trying to lock the final approach for air-gapped packaging and upgrades. TL;DR: proposal A (signed delta bundles + verifier at install-time) vs proposal B (full-image signed artifacts + atomic swap). Any strong objections?
Maya Li: I'm +1 for signed delta bundles to reduce bandwidth, but we need a robust verifier model. Who holds the root key for on-prem installs? :thinking:
Jonah Park: For many customers we'll need an option: root key managed by customer KMS vs Redwood-signed root cert shipped in appliance. Different trust models.
Ravi Singh: Important: rollback semantics. Deltas are smaller but harder to roll back if we don't keep previous full checkpoint on disk. Needs space planning.
Maya Li: Agree on rollback. Proposal: keep N previous images (configurable), apply deltas to a staged dir, run a smoke test, then switch symlink atomically.
Sam Carter: That maps to Proposal A flow: delta -> stage -> verify signatures + attest -> smoke -> swap. Questions: attest where? hardware enclave or local verifier binary?
Maya Li: Prefer local verifier binary with hardware-backed keys where available (TPM/HSM). Enclave option optional. We should avoid mandatory enclaves for smaller customers.
Jonah Park: Another tradeoff: streaming delta apply vs full download. Streaming reduces peak disk use but complicates verification since signatures over whole payload are needed. Could use chunked signatures (tree of signatures).
Ravi Singh: Chunked signatures sound good. Example: sign chunk hashes and then sign the merkle root. Verifier can verify as chunks arrive.
Sam Carter: Sketch of manifest proto I was thinking (example only):

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "artifact_type": "delta",
  "base_version": "2025-02-12-3",
  "chunks": [ { "offset": 0, "len": 1048576, "hash": "sha256:..." }, ... ],
  "signatures": { "root": "sig:...", "chunk_tree": "sig:..." }
}
```

Maya Li: Looks reasonable. We should include an attestations array for metadata (build pipeline ID, rebuild hash, signer key ID) so customers can tie to internal CI.
Jonah Park: Operational concern: how do we deliver bundles to fully air-gapped sites? Options: USB drive, vendor-delivered tarball, mirror via import node. Need a reproducible import tool with integrity checks.
Ravi Singh: We also need a clear operator UX for emergency rollback. Something like `rwi upgrade --rollback-to <version>` that validates the target and verifies signatures locally before switching.
Sam Carter: Good. Also need to decide on DB migrations. For non-reversible migrations we must block automatic rollbacks or require explicit migration down scripts. Add to RFC.
Maya Li: Suggest we support a preflight hook that can run migration dry-run against snapshot. If migration is destructive, abort and require manual approval.
Jonah Park: For long-term refactor: split upgrade logic into two components: "transporter" (gets artifact into the appliance) and "apply-agent" (verify + apply). Makes airgap import vs hosted delivery orthogonal.
Sam Carter: Nice boundary. Transporter could be pluggable (s3-import, usb, http-proxy). Apply-agent enforces verification and the atomic swap.
Ravi Singh: Tests: we need a matrix (small/large disk, low-memory, interrupted power during apply, corrupted chunk mid-stream). Infra bot should run these in CI + hardware-in-the-loop.
InfraBot: CI job created: airgap-upgrade-matrix. Link: https://ci.redwood/steps/airgap-upgrade-matrix/1825 (runs nightly)
Maya Li: One more: make sure telemetry for upgrade failures doesn't leak customer data. We should only send error codes + hashes, not payloads.
Sam Carter: Agreed. Action items:
- Maya: draft verifier API + attestation schema
- Jonah: implement transporter/apply-agent separation doc
- Ravi: define rollback CLI and migration policy
- Infra: add CI tests and HIL plan

Any blockers or objections? If none, I'll update the RFC and schedule design review next Tue.
Maya Li: No blockers from my side. :+1:
Jonah Park: No blockers.
Ravi Singh: No blockers. One ask: add explicit disk-space precheck step in the document.
Sam Carter: Will add it. Thanks everyone!
